item.title: Youth Hub: Orange Shirt Day Beaded Pin Workshop — Mon Sep 28, 4:00 PM — Northern District
item.description:
Orange Shirt Day and National Day for Truth and Reconciliation are observed annually on September 30. In this workshop, Brianna Patrick, Objiway beading artist, will explain the significance of Orange Shirt Day and guide participants in the creation of individual Orange Shirt Day pins that raise awareness and recognize the historical and ongoing trauma that Indigenous peoples experience as a result of the residential school system. Presenter will be virtual, but program is in person. All teens are welcome! Drop-in, no registration required. This program is part of Youth Hub service. item.title: NEW EVENT - 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown — Thu Oct 1, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! # 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown
### A 90-Minute Evening Ghost Walk Through One of Toronto’s Most Historic Neighbourhoods
Cabbagetown has beautiful Victorian houses, quiet streets, old cemeteries, and a history that goes back generations. It also has ghosts.
Join me for a **90-minute evening walking tour through Cabbagetown**, where we'll explore some of the neighbourhood's strangest stories, unsettling legends, and darker pieces of Toronto's past.
We'll begin beneath the glass of **Allan Gardens**, then make our way through the streets of Cabbagetown, stopping along the way for stories of mysterious creatures, haunted buildings, old prisons, cemeteries, restless spirits, and the people who may never have quite left. This isn't a traditional history walk.

item.description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup Join our APAC time-zone friendly virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.
**Time, Date and Location**
Oct 1, 2026 6:00 PM - 8:00 PM PDT Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/apac-ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-october-1-2026)**
**Beyond Exact Matches: Detecting Modified 3D Assets at Marketplace Scale**
How can a marketplace identify copied 3D assets when their orientation, geometry, or composition has changed? Drawing on my work in 3D content understanding at Roblox, this talk will explore multi-view and rotation-invariant representations for similarity and duplicate detection, including the challenges posed by deformed and fragmented copies. It will examine how geometric and semantic signals can complement one another, and discuss practical trade-offs in evaluating detection quality and deploying these methods at scale. item.title: Nuit Blanche 2026 — Sat Oct 3, 7:00 PM — Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
item.description: Join us in celebrating Nuit Blanche’s 20 th anniversary – a free all-night celebration of contemporary art that transforms Toronto’s public spaces into unexpected landscapes and animates cultural sites throughout the city. This year’s theme, Tomorrow’s Memories , invites you to look back to the artists, curators, communities and places that defined Nuit Blanche and its twenty-year history. The Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre (JCCC) Gallery's fall exhibition, Paradise , debuts at Nuit Blanche with an Artist Talk and interactive Origami Frog workshop. Paradise is a multimedia installation by Japanese Canadian artists and longtime family friends Mitchell Akiyama and Emma Nishimura that explores intergenerational inheritance. The JCCC will also host building and museum tours, audio and guided tours, screenings of the unveiling of the Japanese Canadian Monument in Victoria, British Columbia, button making, origami, lantern workshops, and more! Learn more at toronto.ca/NuitBlanche . Schedu
